note: Written; validate_items.R --table-sets passes (44/44 items, resp 1/1.5/2/2.5/3/3.5/4). Caveats. (1) PARENT PROTOCOL, not the child one: the S2 File carries a separate Parent's Protocol version of this closed-ended questionnaire and that is what ships. Its instructions are a self-administered written rubric with no faces card and no bag of pictures; its response anchors are only the two endpoints it names (resp 1 'strongly disagree', resp 4 'strongly agree'), so the children's four-expressive-faces card (1 a lot / 2 a little disagreement, 3 a little / 4 a lot agreement) was deliberately NOT carried over -- the Measures section attributes that card to children specifically. All eleven statements were diffed against the child form: exactly one differs, (viii) '...the world makes him things difficult' (parent) vs '...makes him think it is difficult' (child), and the parent reading ships verbatim, odd grammar included. The four section_prompt stimulus descriptions likewise come from the parent protocol's own open-ended section ('Paolo is autistic and he does not understand what others say', against the child protocol's 'and does not understand'). (2) GENDER OF THE STIMULI, same limitation as the child sibling: the codebook prints the statements once as 'Statements (n = 11 x 2 masculine and x 2 feminine): (Masculine) ...', so only the masculine set is published, while two of the four targets are female (Maria, blind = SD; Elena, able-bodied = ND) and were administered in feminine form. The masculine wording is shipped for all 44 rows rather than a gender-swapped rendering IRW would have written; see public_note. (3) Administered in Italian to Italian parents in Perugia; no Italian wording exists anywhere in the article or S1-S4 (S2 re-checked this round: zero Italian function words, no non-ASCII beyond typographic punctuation; S1 holds only numbers and ASCII column names), so text_source=translated_substitute with translation_source=study_supplied, language=Italian and empty _translated columns. (4) mapping_basis=paper_order, Step 5b routes 3 + 8, status PARTIAL. The four target blocks need no inference (the item code IS the S1 column name for parent rows Protocol 101-199); what is inferred is statement (i)..(xi) -> DEQ1..DEQ11. Route 3 is stronger here than for the child table: Fig 2's published parent means 1.45 / 2.56 / 2.16 for the individual / social / biopsychosocial models are reproduced as 1.460 / 2.584 / 2.178 by blocks 1-4 / 5-7 / 8-11, the best of 35 contiguous partitions by 3.5x. It still cannot separate 8 from 9 (the same clauses reversed), 1 from 3, or pin 5 and 11. (5) resp 1.5/2/2.5/3/3.5 carry no label in the parent protocol, so option_text is deliberately blank there, never padded with the number. Note this differs from the child table, where 2 and 3 ARE labelled by the faces card. (6) Typographic apostrophes and quotes rendered as ASCII and the trailing period on statement (xi) dropped; no other character was changed.
